transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Das (Redwood SE), Avery Chen (Redwood CSM), Evan Brooks (BlueSail Head of ML), Marta Ruiz (Infra Lead), Samir Patel (CTO)

Auto-generated Summary (may be imperfect):
- Discussed per-token pricing and how different deployment modes change unit economics.
- Covered batching, KV cache (sometimes transcribed as KV cash), and quantization as levers.
- Customer concerned about monthly budget cap and latency SLOs.
- Next steps: pricing sheet, benchmark POC, sample prompts.

--- Transcript body ---
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time, um this is Jordan from Redwood, my colleague Priya the SE's on, and Avery from CS. Can you all hear us ok?
[00:06] Evan: Yep, loud and clear. Evan here. Thanks, Jordan.
[00:09] Marta: Marta. All good.
[00:11] Samir: Samir on.
[00:13] Jordan: Awesome. Quick agenda, we'll do a short qualification, dig into your workloads and volumes, then Priya will walk through the cost levers and economics for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private, then we can map to your budget. Sound good?
[00:24] Evan: Perfect. To kick off, we're building some assistant features for our quant research platform — a mixture of short chat requests and longer analysis prompts. Typical request is 800-1,500 tokens per convo, some longer 4k token analysis jobs. We're targeting ~50 qps peak but average closer to 10 qps. Monthly token estimate around 400M tokens. Budget's, uh, rough — we'd like to keep infra + inference under $30k/month if possible.
[00:49] Priya: Cool, that's helpful. Quick clarifying Qs: are those tokens input only, or input + output?
[00:55] Evan: Input + output together, so the 400M is total tokens.
[00:58] Priya: Got it. And latency SLO?
[01:01] Marta: For interactive stuff we want <200ms p50 and <400ms p95 if feasible; for analysis jobs they can be a couple seconds.
[01:08] Jordan: Ok, good. So two workload profiles: interactive low-latency, and batchy analysis. On pricing — Redwood Hosted typical published per-1k-token rates vary by model, but ballpark for a large open-ish model you'd see around $0.30–$0.60 per 1k tokens depending on model size and feature set. Dedicated reserved capacity can materially reduce that; with a committed pool and good batching you can get effective per-1k-token cost down to maybe $0.12–$0.30 depending on utilization and quantization. Private (VPC / on-prem) has similar unit compute economics to Dedicated but you also take on infra and ops costs.
[01:46] Samir: Ok can you break down where that delta comes from? Like what's driving the 2-3x improvement?
[01:51] Priya: Sure — it's a combination of three main levers: batching, caching (prefix/KV cache), and model/quantization. Batching increases GPU utilization so you amortize the per-request overhead and kernel dispatch. For many workloads we see batching cut per-token inference cost by 20–50% depending on latency constraints. KV caching — if you have repeated context or multi-turn sessions, caching the prefix or KV saves you sending the same tokens and recomputing attention, sometimes reducing token consumption by 30–80% for session-heavy use cases. And quantization (4-bit/8-bit) reduces memory and can let you pack more concurrent lanes on GPU, lowering $/token.
[02:26] Evan: When you say batching helps, how does that map to latency? Our interactive p95 requirement is pretty tight.
[02:31] Priya: Right — there's a tradeoff. For interactive strict latency we keep batch sizes small and rely more on fast routes; that limits batching gains. But Redwood routing can split traffic: route interactive to low-latency nodes (slightly higher unit cost) and batch analysis jobs to high-throughput nodes. Also we can do dynamic batching with strict tail latency SLOs — the runtime will only wait a couple ms to collect a small batch. We often recommend a hybrid: Hosted for initial test or lower commitment, Dedicate for predictable high-volume to unlock batching/quantization savings.
[02:58] Marta: Can you quantify savings at 50 qps and 400M tokens/month? Samir: our CFO will ask.
[03:03] Jordan: Sure, rough math — if you ran fully Hosted and assume $0.40 per 1k tokens, 400M tokens is 400,000 * $0.40 = $160k/month, which is above your target. If you move to Dedicated with good utilization and batching, say effective $0.18 per 1k tokens, that's 400,000 * $0.18 = $72k/month. Then apply caching: if session-level caching reduces token issuance by 40% you'd get to ~24k/month effective inference cost, which would be within your $30k target. So caching + dedicated can be a big delta.
[03:36] Evan: Whoa the caching effect — is that realistic? Our assistant does reuse prompts a lot, but not always.
[03:42] Priya: It depends on your convo structure. For example if you have standard system + few-shot prompt that repeats each time, we can keep that prefix in the KV cache on the server and only send deltas. Also for multi-turn assistants the KV cache keeps the long-term keys on GPU so you don't re-encode everything. Typical session-based savings we've seen range widely; we suggested you send a sample prompt set and we'll estimate expected cache hit rate.
[04:02] Samir: There's also question of model choice — do we need the very largest model or smaller tuned models?
[04:07] Priya: Great point — smaller or distilled models do much better on cost; often they give acceptable quality for many retrieval-augmented or structured tasks. Redwood's catalog includes model variants and quantized builds. Also we can suggest a hybrid routing: heavy LLMs only for long analysis jobs, smaller ones for quick tasks.
[04:23] Jordan: On Dedicated economics we also have commit tiers — monthly reserved GPU pools. If you're willing to commit to a baseline throughput we can price the pool such that your marginal $/1k tokens is much lower. There's also burst capacity with pay-as-you-go above the commit.
[04:36] Marta: And private deploy? If we need VPC or on-prem for compliance, how different is the cost?
[04:41] Priya: Private gives you control and data residency but you run at similar raw compute costs. The main difference is you own the infra & ops, so your total cost includes server depreciation, network, and ops people. For some customers with existing infra the per-token compute is similar to Dedicated after amortization, but support and upgrades shift to you. We also offer a Private package where Redwood manages the control plane but you host the inference nodes.
[05:02] Evan: Security-wise we need SOC2 type 2, SSO, SAML, KMS, and audit trails — do you have that?
[05:08] Avery: Yes, Redwood is SOC2, supports SAML/SSO, integrates with customer KMS/HSM for key management, and we provide audit logs. We'll share the docs.
[05:16] Samir: Great. Back to pricing mechanics, can you show an interactive cost model? CFO wants to see the sensitivity to QPS, cache hit rate, and token lengths.
[05:24] Jordan: Absolutely — I'll send an interactive spreadsheet but Priya will do a couple of quick configs: 50 qps interactive profile with small batches and 10 qps averaged analysis profile with large batches.
[05:33] Priya: For rough bench math, assume 50 qps with 1k average tokens/request that's 3M tokens/hour peak — yeah that aligns with your monthly. If we enable batching and use 4-bit quantization on Dedicated we get lower per-token. We'll run an estimate with your prompt shapes and give a best/likely/worst case.
[05:51] Evan: One more on caching — does the KV cache require sticky routing to keep sessions on same node?
[05:55] Priya: Good question. We have sticky routing plus a global cache layer. For most use cases the session sticks to a node for the duration of a short session; for resilience we can fallback and rebuild cache. There's some tradeoff between global consistency and caching hit rate. We'll outline options in the doc.
[06:10] Marta: If we wanted to pilot, how quickly can we spin up a Dedicated pool?
[06:13] Jordan: We can spin up a small dedicated pool within a week for a POC, depending on GPU availability. Hosted trial is immediate. For the POC we recommend 2 weeks of benchmarks: sample prompts, traffic replay, and then tune batching/caching.
[06:24] Samir: On billing — do you do blended billing for Dedicated vs Hosted?
[06:28] Jordan: You can have hybrid billing — some workloads on Hosted, others on Dedicated. We'll show blended forecasts in the cost model.
[06:33] Evan: We'd like to see a scenario where we hit our $30k target without sacrificing the p95 latency too much.
[06:39] Priya: That's doable on paper if you get a ~40% effective cache hit and route interactive carefully. But we need your real prompt set to model it properly.
[06:47] Jordan: Quick aside — have you evaluated any competitors for this project?
[06:50] Evan: We talked to Anthropic and tried their hosted route, and we looked at some managed endpoints on Vertex. Also brief eval of running on-prem with open-source stacks.
[06:58] Priya: Good notes. Redwood typically competes on predictable economics and tooling for rollouts and monitoring — so you'll get per-route cost breakdowns and token-level traces.
[07:07] Marta: Any hidden costs to watch for? Network egress? Storage for embeddings?
[07:11] Jordan: Yes, network egress if you host across regions, large embedding storage if you persist vectors, and data retention if you need long term logging. We'll call those out in the cost model.
[07:19] Evan: For the POC — we want to validate: 1) can we meet p95 <400ms for interactive, 2) hit <$30k/mo with our volumes, 3) ensure SOC2/KMS integration.
[07:30] Jordan: Nice crisp success criteria. We'll map them to the POC.
[07:33] Priya: Ok let's get into a little more detail on the batching numbers — for example, for non-strict interactive we can use a 16-32 token headroom to queue and form micro-batches; that usually gives a 20–35% cost reduction without hurting p95 significantly. For long analysis tasks we go larger, like batch sizes of 8–32 requests to maximize GPU throughput.
[07:55] Samir: What's the expected utilization threshold where Dedicated becomes better than Hosted?
[07:58] Priya: It varies but rule-of-thumb: if you're sustaining a high baseline (hundreds of tokens/sec or tens of thousands of tokens/min consistently), Dedicated with commit unlocks savings. With your 400M/mo and steady patterns, Dedicated looks favorable once caching and batching are applied.
[08:12] Evan: Could you also show an example of how quantization changes performance? We worry about QA/regression on outputs.
[08:16] Priya: Absolutely — quantization often has slight quality regressions on edge-case reasoning tasks; we'll run evals on your prompt set. We can also recommend a mixed strategy: quantized smaller model for most traffic, full-precision for high-value analysis.
[08:28] Marta: Are there any licensing or IP issues with models on private infra?
[08:31] Jordan: Depends on the model license; for open models it's generally fine, but we track lic issues during onboarding. We'll note model licensing considerations in the docs.
[08:39] Evan: Ok let's talk timeline — if we do a POC starting 3/9, 2 weeks bench, then a decision by end of March does that sound reasonable?
[08:46] Jordan: Yes, that's reasonable. We'll prepare the POC plan and required artifacts.
[08:50] Samir: One more ops question: if we do Private with Redwood control plane, what's the upgrade/ticket SLA?
[08:56] Avery: For Private customers we offer enterprise support tiers. We can go over SLA specifics in the contract phase. We'll include a support summary in the pack.
[09:04] Evan: Great. Anything else from your side?
[09:06] Priya: I'll note to run a simulated 50 qps bench with these prompt shapes and vary cache hit rate from 0% to 60% so you can see sensitivity.
[09:15] Jordan: Perfect. We'll also add a blended forecast for Hosted+Dedic+Private scenarios and call out break-even utilization points.
[09:22] Marta: Please include network/egress and storage in the cost table.
[09:25] Jordan: Will do.
[09:27] Evan: Thanks — that was super helpful.
[09:30] Jordan: Ok quick recap and next steps: Jordan will send pricing sheet + cost model; Priya will run bench and share per-token estimates for the configs discussed; BlueSail will send sample prompts and volume breakdown; schedule POC kickoff next week. We'll also attach SOC2 + KMS integration docs.
[09:48] Samir: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[09:51] Jordan: Thanks all, we'll follow up by Friday.

[End of transcript — rough alignment with 42 minute call; timestamps uneven due to auto-timestamps. Some transcription artifacts: KV cash, Dedicate, quan-tization etc may appear in auto text.]
